stages.label: Memory residency + mapping
stages.scope: Earlier P020 hardware with the qualified N16 mapping family and resident memory policy. This base group includes the inherited datapath; it is not an isolated memory-only effect.

stages.label: Hardware refinement
stages.scope: Combined WO23 and WO24 hardware refinements under the pre-fusion N16 family: earlier-hardware N16 control to selected WO24 hardware with producer fusion, prefetch and the second context disabled. Compatible mappings may be reselected. The intervening WO23 point is retained explicitly; no software-menu expansion is credited as hardware.

stages.label: Producer-layout fusion
stages.scope: Enable rounded attention producer-layout storage fusion; no cross-wave prefetch or second accumulator.

stages.label: Cross-wave prefetch
stages.scope: Enable paid cross-wave prefetch while retaining producer fusion and one FP32 accumulator context.

stages.label: Compute/readout overlap
stages.scope: Add the second FP32 context with fusion and prefetch retained. Original output conversion, stores and reduction order remain paid. The simple label denotes next-tile compute overlapping prior-result readout using the second FP32 context; bulk conversion and output stores remain charged.

slices.label: Placement / residency†
slices.scope: Earlier P020 hardware with the qualified N16 mapping family and resident memory policy. This base group includes the inherited datapath; it is not an isolated memory-only effect.

slices.label: Hardware resources
slices.scope: Combined WO23 and WO24 hardware refinements under the pre-fusion N16 family: earlier-hardware N16 control to selected WO24 hardware with producer fusion, prefetch and the second context disabled. Compatible mappings may be reselected. The intervening WO23 point is retained explicitly; no software-menu expansion is credited as hardware.

slices.label: Fusion / storage
slices.scope: Enable rounded attention producer-layout storage fusion; no cross-wave prefetch or second accumulator.

slices.label: Scheduling / concurrency
slices.scope: Sum of sequential cross-wave prefetch and compute/readout-overlap increments. This does not add overlapping feature-off ablations; original paid costs are unchanged.

stages.label: Resident datapath + KV
stages.scope: Joint resident custom datapath: final memory capacity, weight and KV retention, original first imports, formats, vector and host resources; old mapping menu. Active arrays capped at 256, DRAM at 900 GB/s and local delivery at 8192 GB/s. Not isolated software and not a TPU-v3 implementation.

stages.label: Tiling extension
stages.scope: Extend 25 to 31 compatible mappings under the same service caps; residency and all owners stay fixed.

stages.label: Array parallelism
stages.scope: Restore selected array availability; DRAM/local caps remain. Compatible mappings may be reselected.

stages.label: DRAM bandwidth
stages.scope: Restore selected delivered DRAM bandwidth, retaining full array availability and the local-service cap.

stages.label: Local delivery bandwidth
stages.scope: Restore selected local delivery bandwidth. This reaches the unchanged selected execution.

method: Partition cumulative increments in S=T_B2/T, starting at S=1. For each Llama resource increase, first retain the previous mapping, then allow compatible remapping. Group the original menu extension and all remapping gains with the on-chip bandwidth gain. Remaining groups are compute parallelism, base memory/residency and DRAM bandwidth.
order_scope: Four display groups per workload. DeepSeek scheduling/concurrency sums its original sequential prefetch and compute/readout-overlap increments. Llama groups, underlying controls, comparison order, final speedups and reference remain unchanged.
footnote: Memory capacity/residency includes inherited base hardware and mapping. It is not an isolated SRAM-capacity gain. SRAM capacity and bank/port reservations are fixed through the Llama tiling and resource comparisons; on-chip bandwidth is local_GBps. DRAM bandwidth refers to external DRAM, not FPGA BRAM.
